item.text: I’m taking another pass with a narrower goal: reduce the remaining incidental complexity rather than just moving code around. I’ll inspect the current sources and then tighten the selection API and tests if there’s still a clean improvement to make.

There’s still one structural improvement worth making: the implementation currently chains mutating helpers in a way that hides the flow, and the tests repeat the same call pattern. I’m refactoring both into clearer, single-purpose helpers without changing the external behavior.
The cleanup is in. I’m recompiling and rerunning the tests now to confirm the helper consolidation didn’t introduce any drift.

Refactored the remaining rough edges in [ActivitySelection.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:1) and [ActivitySelectionTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelectionTest.java:1). The implementation now uses a single `toSortedActivities(...)` step instead of chaining mutating helpers, which makes the flow easier to follow. I also added `Activity.toString()` so internal objects are easier to inspect if this grows further.

The test harness is now less repetitive: selection assertions go through a shared `SelectionCase` helper, so adding new behavior checks is simpler and less error-prone.
